ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three mutually overlapping circular rings, with six intersection points marked by small circles in total. The number 6 is already marked in the small circle at the bottom; the small circle with the question mark is located at the upper intersection point of the two lower circular rings. The upper circular ring passes through the other four small circles, but does not pass through the question mark position and the bottom 6. Reasoning: Let the number at the question mark be x. The numbers 1 to 6 are each used once, and the total sum is 1+2+3+4+5+6=21. Each small circle is on the intersection point of two circular rings, so when adding the sums of the numbers on the three circular rings, each number will be counted twice; therefore the total sum of the three circular rings is 2×21=42. The sums of the three circular rings are the same, so the sum of each circular ring is 42÷3=14. The upper circular ring contains the four numbers other than x and 6, so its sum is 21-6-x=15-x. Thus 15-x=14, solving gives x=1.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: there are three overlapping rings with six circled pairwise intersection points. The bottom circled point is 6, and the question mark is the upper intersection of the two lower rings. The upper ring passes through the other four circled points and not through the question mark or the 6. Let the question mark be x. From the text, the numbers 1 through 6 are used once, so their total is 21, and all three ring sums are equal. Since each circled intersection lies on exactly two rings, adding the three ring sums counts every number twice, giving total 42; hence each ring sum is 42/3 = 14. The upper ring contains exactly the four numbers other than x and 6, so its sum is 21 - 6 - x = 15 - x. Set 15 - x = 14 to get x = 1.

method.method_draft: First describe the image by grouping the circles by rings. Let x be the question mark. Let P be the sum of the two circled points where the lower-left ring meets the upper ring, and let Q be the sum of the two circled points where the lower-right ring meets the upper ring. The image shows the upper ring contains exactly those four points, so its sum is P + Q. The lower-left ring contains P plus the shared lower-ring intersections x and 6, so its sum is P + x + 6. The lower-right ring contains Q plus x and 6, so its sum is Q + x + 6. Since all three ring sums are equal, P + Q = P + x + 6, so Q = x + 6, and P + Q = Q + x + 6, so P = x + 6. Therefore P + Q = 2x + 12. But P + Q is also the sum of the four numbers other than x and 6, namely 21 - x - 6 = 15 - x. Solve 15 - x = 2x + 12 to get x = 1.
